# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the EXACT tasks you broke/fixed) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — prompt: forbid formulas/macros, force literal values, generalize code, match type/format
- Changes I made (all in prompt.md; system-prompt is the only editable artifact — no tools.py):
  - Cluster 1 (BEHAVIORAL, biggest): added a hard "Write COMPUTED LITERAL VALUES — never formulas or macros" section with rationale (grader reads stored cell values, not evaluated formulas) + a worked From/serial example. Reframes "use a formula/macro/VBA/SUMIFS/INDEX-MATCH" as "produce the RESULT". Targets 40467, 374-9, 32468 where the agent stored a `=`-formula and scored 0.
  - Cluster 2 (KNOWLEDGE+BEHAVIORAL): added "Make your code GENERAL — it may be re-run on other data": detect real last row/col dynamically, match columns/rows by header text, never hardcode counts or paste sample values. Targets partial-credit/flaky (53161, 374-9, 418-29, 52216) that only fit the sample file.
  - Cluster 3 (KNOWLEDGE): added "Match the expected data type and format" + reproduce already-filled template cells in the answer range. Targets 40467 (text) and 52216 (C15:G15 template).
  - Cluster 4 (KNOWLEDGE, conditional): "Preserve everything outside the target" — ONLY when multi-sheet OR data not at A1, edit in place with openpyxl instead of rebuilding from a DataFrame. Targets 347-49/32468/374-9.
- Expected effect + why safe: only guaranteed-passing task is 47484 (single-sheet, data at A1, writes literal text "01" via pandas groupby, no formulas). Every new rule either doesn't apply to it (cluster-4 condition is false) or matches what it already does (clusters 1/2/3) → its trajectory/output is unchanged. No passing trial in any task ever wrote a formula, so the no-formula rule cannot flip a passing behavior.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — first iteration after baseline seed (LEDGER shows baseline only; prior_iterations empty).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: 55457 (instruction field is empty/nbsp — unfixable by general prompt without hardcoding); 347-49 exact blank-row-deletion semantics (ambiguous). Designs tried: none for these yet.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration). If cluster-2 generalization gains little next time, switch lever toward per-failure interpretation scaffolding (explicit inspect-then-verify checklist) rather than more global rules.
- Focus next iteration: if accepted, measure which clusters moved; if 374-9/53161 still partial, add a concrete "re-read the answer range width and fill ALL of it" verification step; consider whether 347-49 needs a worked deletion example.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.540 Δ=+0.147 · fixed={160-6, 52216, 53161} · broke={—}.

## Iteration cand_0002 — prompt: teach READING formula cells via data_only; forbid hardcoded base / fixed inter-row step
- Changes I made (both in prompt.md; system-prompt is the only editable artifact):
  - Edit 1 (cluster: reading formula cells): new "Reading cells that contain formulas" section — openpyxl default `.value` on a `=`-cell returns the formula TEXT, so `isinstance(v,(int,float))` skips it / treats as 0; open a SECOND `data_only=True` handle to read computed values, keep the normal handle for saving, never treat a `=`-string as 0/blank; worked date example. Targets 374-9 (source `=SUM(...)` cells) and 40467 (B/C/A formulas).
  - Edit 2 (cluster: hardcoded base / fixed step): added a rule under "Make your code GENERAL" — derive each output from that row's own source inputs; never hardcode an observed base value or assume a fixed inter-row step (e.g. +7/day). Targets 40467 t0 which hardcoded 2023-12-31 + 7*(row-1) → cases 2,3 = 0.
- Expected effect + why safe: 374-9 should rise from mostly-0 (formula-skipping) toward the data_only trial's partial-or-better, consistently; 40467 should stop the flaky hardcoded-base failures. Both are ADDITIVE, CONDITIONAL knowledge — passing tasks 47484/52216/53161/160-6 read plain values (52216's only formulas are outside its answer range), so neither rule changes their trajectory. No global decision/permission rule touched. Blast radius BOUNDED.
- Building on prior RESULTS: cand_0001 ACCEPTED (val 0.540, fixed 160-6/52216/53161). Kept all its rules intact; added the READING-formulas knowledge it lacked (cand_0001 only covered WRITING literals, not reading formula results — the actual root cause of 374-9/40467's formula skipping).
- Refuted hypotheses: none disproven yet (only one prior iteration, accepted).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: 55457 (empty nbsp instruction — unfixable generally); 32468 (12-month rolling-window/sign semantics from DISCOUNT tab — source is plain numeric so data_only inapplicable; need ground truth to pin window inclusivity/sign); 347-49 (exact blank-rows-to-delete-above-"Gross Pay" set is ambiguous). Designs tried for these: none safe without overfitting.
- Plateau signal: n/a (2nd iteration). If data_only gains little, the remaining fixable clusters (32468/347-49) are SEMANTIC-interpretation gaps — next lever would be a worked example per semantic pattern (rolling window inclusivity; row-deletion + compaction) rather than more mechanics.
- Focus next iteration: if accepted, check whether 374-9 reached full pass or is still capped by uncached data_only formulas (2,3); if capped, that class needs formula EVALUATION (out of prompt scope). Attempt 32468 window/sign only if a trace reveals the intended semantics.
